assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and the Sr lattice clock that followed turned optical lattice trapping into a clock architecture with fractional uncertainty at or below 1e-18. This is a clearly identifiable discovery/invention with lasting impact on timekeeping, geodesy, fundamental-constant tests and dark-matter searches.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrations; Ye drove the many-atom, spin-polarised Sr clock to the lowest systematic uncertainties and the frequency-comb link. Two laureates is a clean configuration. Other contributors (e.g. Takamoto, Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley) and the single-ion clock lineage are not credited here, so the boundary with the 2005 comb prize and ion clocks needs care.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than twenty years of independent confirmation at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and others, with stable interpretation. Timing is good, and the redefinition of the second makes recognition natural now.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to distinguish lattice clocks from single-ion optical clocks and from the comb work already recognised in 2005.
Allocation between Katori and Ye, and whether a third person from the broader clock community should be considered, is not settled by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration of round electron lenses overcame a limit that Scherzer showed in 1936 could not be removed with rotationally symmetric lenses. It brought routine sub-angstrom resolution and atomic-resolution spectroscopy, and transformed materials and condensed-matter physics. The discovery/invention is concrete and its impact is broad and durable. My own field is electron microscopy, so I flag a potential perceived conflict and have tried to judge it against the same criteria as the others.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theory of aberration-correcting multipole optics, Haider built and demonstrated the TEM corrector with Urban and Rose in the late 1990s, and Urban led its application to materials, so the three-person configuration is defensible. Credit for the STEM corrector (Krivanek, Dellby, Batson) is not in the supplied names, and that unresolved allocation is a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Mature: aberration-corrected TEM and STEM are installed across the world and widely confirmed. Recognition is overdue rather than premature, though much of the impact is enabling-instrument impact in materials science and may be judged more as chemistry or materials than physics.
uncertainties: The omission of the STEM-corrector pioneers from the supplied credit may make the configuration unfair.
Physics versus chemistry/materials fit, given prior recognition through the Wolf and Kavli prizes in other settings.
I am a microscopist and my assessment may be coloured by that proximity; I cannot verify specific factual details beyond my own knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators opened a whole class of topological quantum matter and transformed band-structure thinking. Kane and Mele's 2005 theory, and the HgTe/CdTe observation of edge transport, have strongly shaped condensed-matter research.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step. Molenkamp's group made the early experimental realisation following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, but Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and Hasan are not among the credited names, so a fair allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of independent confirmation in HgTe, Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3 with ARPES and transport. Recognition is timely, with the topological-phase prize of 2016 already awarded for related physics.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize and the unresolved credit for the HgTe proposal and for three-dimensional topological insulators.
Credit may be better configured with names outside the supplied set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical-lattice quantum simulation turned the Hubbard model and quantum phase transitions into controllable laboratory experiments, and quantum-gas microscopy brought single-site resolution. Impact on many-body physics is deep and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, Greiner, Bloch and Hänsch demonstrated the superfluid-Mott transition, and Esslinger's fermionic work is also decisive. A three-name cap forces a hard choice that the supplied credit does not resolve.
assessment.maturity: Mature in experiment, but the programme is still evolving toward analogue and digital quantum simulation, and the strongest long-term results may still be to come.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Esslinger and the earlier Hänsch/Jaksch contributions.
Overlap with the 2001 and 1997 cold-atom prizes and the broader quantum-simulation field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened moire quantum materials, a rapidly growing area with clear conceptual novelty.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key prediction in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experiment. Cao and others who did the experiments are not credited, and Kim, Dean and Young groups also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Strongly and independently confirmed, but young: moire physics is still developing, so the interpretation of the superconductivity is not yet settled. Recognition might be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Credit for graduate-student and postdoctoral experimenters beyond the three credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a genuine invention that uses engineered intersubband transitions in heterostructures to give unipolar mid-infrared lasers. It rests on band-gap engineering and molecular beam epitaxy and has had wide use in spectroscopy and sensing.
assessment.attribution: Capasso conceived the cascade concept and led the Bell Labs team, Faist demonstrated the device in 1994, and Cho supplied the MBE growth. Others at Bell Labs (Sirtori, Sivco, Hutchinson) also contributed, and earlier Kazarinov-Suris proposals complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of independent development, with room-temperature continuous-wave operation and commercial adoption. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority of the earlier Kazarinov and Suris theoretical proposal.
Whether the work is best seen as physics or as device engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision model and its quantum theory explain high-harmonic generation and underlie attosecond pulse generation. Having chaired the 2023 cycle, I note the work was not credited then, and it is the conceptual foundation of that field.
assessment.attribution: Corkum's 1993 model and Schafer's concurrent work gave the semiclassical picture, and Lewenstein's 1994 theory gave the quantum treatment. Credit is genuinely shared and ordering is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed in many labs, but the 2023 prize already honoured the attosecond experiments, which raises timing and overlap questions.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 prize and whether the committee would see the model as a separate discovery.
Allocation among Corkum, Schafer, Lewenstein and others such as Kulander.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light allows measurements below the standard quantum limit. Caves proposed its use in interferometers, and its deployment in gravitational-wave detectors shows clear practical impact.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the theory, Kimble made early experimental demonstration of squeezing, and Schnabel advanced practical squeezed-light sources for detectors. Many others (Slusher, Walls, Mavalvala, McKenzie, Vahlbruch) contributed, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature in demonstration and in use at LIGO and Virgo, but the discovery is spread over four decades and many groups.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse and the four credited names cannot all be accommodated.
